issues.description: prediction_program.R unconditionally reads Data_ML_M2.csv for the month-by-month branch, but no supplied source exports or otherwise produces that exact table. Its fields, identifiers and month-index contract are not defined.

prediction_program_H.R unconditionally reads Data_ML_H_Scenario.csv, but no supplied source exports or otherwise produces that exact table. The file is copied to a second object but the object has no later use; the authored script still requires the read to succeed.

prediction_program_H.R concatenates predictions by officer_index and builds data_officer_reorder in that grouped order, but line 104 attaches the prediction vector to the original data_officer object. The supplied sources do not establish the input row order or the intended application-key alignment, so no reordering repair is inferred.

The officer GBM fit removes column 2 from Data_ML_H.csv while its formula names loan_size_signed. The supplied export selects named fields but does not establish the file's full source-column order; the exact field removed by -2 and the intended exclusion remain unknown.

R writes prediction columns with dotted names (human.gbm.pred, gbm.pred and ols.pred), while Stata keeps dot-free names (humangbmpred, gbmpred and olspred). Stata 18 documents name normalization on delimited import but not the exact mapping for these headers; no alias repair is supported without the actual mapping.

model.do actively labels and graphs period and the profit_rate_*_dt series at lines 450-474, but none of the included Stata or R programs creates or imports those fields. Their producer, record order, period definition and compatible input are not supplied.

The local macros contain i.-prefixed factor-variable terms and are expanded inside keep varlists at model.do lines 213-214 and 329. Stata 18 documentation says factor variables are accepted by most estimation/postestimation commands and a few other commands, while the keep entry specifies varlist syntax; that documentation does not establish this exact command/notation combination. No syntax trial or replacement is proposed.

Both R scripts set their working directory to a Windows G: path. The package's R runtime is [redacted-path-c341561b0702]; use one declared relative working root for the shared Stata/R intermediates in a working copy.

evidence.description: The H prediction vector is appended in increasing officer_index order.
evidence.quote:
human.gbm.pred <- c()
for(i in 1:max(data_officer2$officer_index)){
  print(i)
  human.gbm <- gbm(
    formula = loan_size_signed ~ . - officer_index,
    distribution = "gaussian",
    data = data_officer2[data_officer2$officer_index == i, -2],
    n.trees = 500,
    interaction.depth = 2,
    shrinkage = 0.1,
    n.minobsinnode = 5,
    bag.fraction = 0.8,
    cv.folds = 5,
    n.cores = NULL, # will use all cores by default
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  gbm.pred <- predict(human.gbm, n.trees = human.gbm$n.trees, 
    data_officer2[data_officer2$officer_index == i, ])
  human.gbm.pred <- c(human.gbm.pred, gbm.pred)
  }
